newsitem.title: albania: Envoy says Albania parties want June 29 election.
newsitem.headline: Envoy says Albania parties want June 29 election.

text.p: International mediator Franz Vranitzky said on Thursday all parties in Albania's national unity government had agreed that election should take place on June 29.

"I have listened to several parties and the government and they are all of the opinion that the elections should take place on June 29," he told reporters. "However, they are not in agreement on the conditions."

Vranitzky, an envoy of the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), spoke to reporters after talks with President Sali Berisha and other leading political figures. He was due to meet Prime Minister Bashkim Fino later.
Berisha agreed last month to hold elections by the end of June, four years early, as an insurrection sparked by the collapse of dubious savings schemes was at its height.
An emergency all-party government was installed headed by Fino, whose Socialist Party had been the main opposition force.
Vranitzky said it appeared parties were not communicating with each other to find a consensus on preparing for the vote.
Berisha said on Wednesday that the rebel committees controlling much of the south of the chaotic Balkan country must be disbanded before the election.
Vranitzky held talks on Thursday with Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu, Finance Minister Arben Malaj and a leading Socialist Party politician Fatos Nano.
He said parties remained divided over how they viewed the self-proclaimed rebel "committees of national salvation".
"That is certainly the hardest part about the whole election process," he said.
The rebels have vowed not to give in until Berisha, a northerner, quits. Rebels accuse him of not intervening to stop the savings schemes, that bankrupted thousands of families when they collapsed.
Parties remain divided on what system should be used to elect the 140-member parliament. Under current rules, 120 seats are elected by majority vote and the rest by proportional representation.

Berisha was returned to power in a May 1996 general election with a landslide victory giving him 122 seats. The Socialists denounced the elections as fraudulent and boycotted the vote. International monitors said the polls were seriously flawed.
